2609.00464.title: Does Reasoning Mitigate Backdoor Attacks? A Neuro-Symbolic Perspective
2609.00464.paper_summary: Neuro-Symbolic (NeSy) AI has recently emerged as a novel paradigm to enable trustworthy AI, aiming at integrating sub-symbolic neural perception with grounded symbolic reasoning. The neuro-symbolic integration process that characterizes these models has been proven beneficial to achieve more transparent, explainable and efficient AI systems. Meanwhile, their properties under adversarial settings have been overlooked being frequently deemed robust-by-design. However, the neural-symbolic integration process they leverage constitutes an additional layer of complexity that may provide an attack entry-point. Therefore, in this paper, we claim that an in-depth investigation of the adversarial robustness of NeSy models is necessary and provide the first systematic evaluation of backdoor attacks against NeSy. To this end, we compare the most popular NeSy framework, namely DeepProbLog, against baseline neural networks across a total of eight backdoor settings and four reasoning tasks. Our experimental results show that while NeSy models are indeed more robust than their neural counterpart on average, their robustness vastly depend on the strictness of the reasoning process being enforced and its compatibility with the chosen adversarial target. The source code to reproduce our experiments is made available at https://github.com/marcoantoniocorallo/NeSy-Backdoor.
2609.00464.paper_summary_zh: 神經符號（NeSy）人工智慧最近出現，成為一種新穎的範式，以實現可信的人工智慧，旨在整合次符號的神經感知與基於實證的符號推理。這些模型所特徵的神經符號整合過程已被證明對於實現更透明、可解釋和高效的人工智慧系統是有益的。與此同時，它們在對抗性環境下的特性卻被忽視，常常被認為是設計上具有穩健性。然而，它們所利用的神經符號整合過程構成了一層額外的複雜性，可能提供攻擊的切入點。因此，在本文中，我們聲稱有必要對NeSy模型的對抗穩健性進行深入調查，並提供對NeSy的後門攻擊的首次系統性評估。為此，我們將最受歡迎的NeSy框架，即DeepProbLog，與基線神經網絡在總共八個後門設置和四個推理任務中進行比較。我們的實驗結果顯示，儘管NeSy模型在平均情況下確實比其神經對應物更具穩健性，但它們的穩健性在很大程度上取決於所施加的推理過程的嚴格性及其與所選對抗目標的兼容性。我們的實驗源代碼可在https://github.com/marcoantoniocorallo/NeSy-Backdoor取得。
